sop_version: SOP 50 10 8.1 (Lender and Development Company Loan Programs with Technical Policy Updates), published 2026-09-25, effective 2026-10-01

min_equity_injection.quote: The following are the minimum equity injection requirements for change of ownership transactions based on their type: Initial Acquisition: 10%.

coverage_change_of_ownership.quote: The Debt Service Coverage (DSC) ratio must be satisfied using either the last fiscal year-end or an average of the last two fiscal year-end statements on either a historical or adjusted basis based on the transaction type: Initial Acquisition: 1.25:1
coverage_change_of_ownership.section: Appendix 15, Para. C.2.b (Lender's Credit Analysis, financial analysis of repayment ability)

max_term_years_no_real_estate.quote: 7(a) loans that facilitate a change of ownership must not have an amortization that exceeds 10 years, except as provided below for transactions involving Special Purpose Properties.

max_loan.quote: The maximum loan amount for any one Standard 7(a) loan is $5,000,000.
max_loan.section: Section B, Ch. 1, Para. B.1 (Maximum Loan Amount, Standard 7(a) loans)

standby_note_max_share_of_injection.quote: The following sources, whether individually or in the aggregate, may provide no more than half of the required Equity Injection. Seller debt that is subordinated to the Lender and on full standby (no payments of principal or interest for the term of the 7(a) loan) may be considered as equity for SBA’s purposes.
standby_note_max_share_of_injection.section: Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a (Source of Equity Injections, Limited Equity Injection Sources: Standby Debt Agreements and Seller Debt)

qoe.quote: For Business Expansion and Initial Acquisition transactions where the Purchase Price as defined in Paragraph A.1 is equal to or greater than $3 million, the Lender must also obtain a Quality of Earnings (QoE) in addition to the required Business Valuation. The $3 million threshold is determined before the application of buyer equity, seller debt, or other financing sources. Owner Buyout and ESOP & Cooperative transactions are not subject to the QoE requirement because the existing owner(s) retain operational knowledge of the business and the transaction does not result in a change to the management or operating structure. The QoE must be performed by an independent, experienced financial professional and must be conducted for the benefit of the Lender. As the QoE report is part of the financial due diligence of the transaction, the report must not be prepared by or for the seller.
qoe.flag_text: When a new owner buys the business at this price, an SBA lender requires an independent Quality of Earnings report. The report must be done for the lender. The seller cannot prepare it or have it prepared.
